rules.title: A startup entry that runs something out of a temporary folder
rules.why: A temporary folder is emptied by the system and by cleaners, so an entry there is one that expects to be re-created rather than installed.
rules.benign: An installer that registers a temporary shim and removes it when it finishes.
rules.remediation: Quarantine the binary, then remove the startup entry.

rules.title: An unsigned startup entry in the user's own scope
rules.why: A signature is a fact about the file, not a verdict: unsigned means the author did not buy a certificate, and nothing more.
rules.benign: A small open-source launcher, or a self-built binary, that has never been signed.
rules.remediation: Open the folder and look at the file before removing anything. The hash is in the finding.

rules.title: A process running from a temporary folder
rules.why: Programs are installed, not left in the folder the system empties; a process there is either passing through or hiding in it.
rules.benign: A portable application that unpacks itself and runs from its own extraction folder.
rules.remediation: Look at the process's parent and command line before acting; the details are in the panel.

rules.title: A socket waiting for a connection on every interface
rules.why: A socket bound to every interface is reachable from the network, which is a decision someone made rather than a default most programs choose.
rules.benign: A development server or a file-sharing program the person started deliberately.
rules.remediation: Close the program, or bind it to loopback in its settings. The owning process is in the row.

rules.title: An editor or agent configuration that names a command to run
rules.why: A configuration that runs a command is a startup path with a different name, and it is read by a program the person trusts.
rules.benign: A task or hook the person wrote themselves in their own editor.
rules.remediation: Read the configuration file the finding names, then remove the hook if you did not write it.
